name: Murf
summary: A voiceover studio for corporate media: pick a voice, edit timing like a document, export finished narration.
description:
Murf is aimed at the person making the training video, not at the developer building a real-time feature. The studio model — voice selection, script editing with pacing control, pronunciation fixes, export aligned to a slide deck — matches how narration actually gets produced in a marketing or L&D team, and the voice library is broad enough to cover most brand tones.

Because it is studio-first, API-and-latency work is a weaker fit, and it is not trying to win cloning either. If the job is a call that responds in under 300ms, look elsewhere; if the job is 40 explainer videos a quarter that sound consistent, this is the shape of tool that fits.
